added_lines: this week we will celebrate christmas day. the birth of jesus christ, over two thousand years ago, was a pivotal moment in the lives of many people at that time, and ever since. in a sense, we join the angels, the shepherds, and the wise men who rejoiced with mary and joseph at the birth of the long awaited saviour of the world.

we join the apostles and the disciples - men and women - who knew jesus personally, who walked with him and worked with him in those early days of spreading the good news of god's love for us in sending his son among us.

we join all those who, down the years and right up to our own time, have lived up to their baptismal promises to be god’s people, living and handing on the faith to the generations coming behind them.

as we gather with family, friends, neighbours, and fellow parishioners for christmas mass and other celebrations, let us pledge ourselves to be a people of faith, hope, and love in a world which needs the presence of jesus christ - through our care, our words, and our actions - now more than ever before.
merry christmas and a very happy new year.
nollaig shona daoibh, agus athbhliain faoi mhaise.
